title: Decentralized Internet Infrastructure
definition: A collective of projects and organizations committed to building a decentralized internet infrastructure that is interoperable, secure, and community-governed.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine the internet as a big playground where everyone has a say and control over their data. This playground is made up of different parts like storage, identity, and retrieval systems. This collective wants to make sure these parts work together and no one part can take over.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: This is a decentralized internet infrastructure initiative that aims to create interoperable standards and protocols for data storage, retrieval, identity, and economic incentives. The infrastructure is governed by a Steward and follows a rough consensus decision-making process.
difficulty_levels.expert: This initiative is a novel exploration of how a collective of projects can create a decentralized internet infrastructure that is both technologically robust and philosophically grounded in principles of interoperability, neutrality, and forkability. It challenges the traditional centralized model of the internet and proposes a more democratic and community-oriented approach. By addressing technical disputes through technical working groups and governance disputes through social enforcement, it highlights the importance of consensus-building and community governance in shaping the future of the internet.

extra_fields.insight: The collective's commitment to building a decentralized internet infrastructure that is interoperable, secure, and community-governed highlights the importance of consensus-building and community governance in shaping the future of the internet.
